paragraphs.heading: F-16 Engine - Turbine Module
paragraphs.text: Interactive Electronic Technical Manual (IETM) for the F-16 engine (turbine module). The manual combines descriptive data, an interactive Illustrated Parts Data (IPD) module and step-by-step procedures, all linked to the 3D model.

paragraphs.heading: How to use
paragraphs.text: Select a data module in the publication tree. Click a part in the 3D view or a row in the parts list to cross-highlight it. Use the viewer toolbar to isolate, hide, x-ray or explode the engine. Add parts to the order list with the cart button.

paragraphs.heading: Safety
paragraphs.text: Engine work is done with the engine on the maintenance stand, cold, drained and with the ignition disarmed. Follow the warnings and cautions in each procedure.

paragraphs.heading: Data status
paragraphs.text: This is a proof-of-concept publication. Part numbers, CAGE codes and procedures are sample data.

paragraphs.heading: General
paragraphs.text: The F-16 is powered by one afterburning turbofan engine. Air flows from the inlet at the front through the compressor, the combustor and the turbine to the exhaust at the rear. Select a heading to isolate that part of the engine in the 3D view: it keeps its own colours and the rest of the engine turns transparent.

paragraphs.heading: Compressor section
paragraphs.text: The inlet guide vanes (120) turn the air onto the fan rotor (110). The compressor stages (130) raise the pressure of the core air before combustion.

paragraphs.heading: Combustion
paragraphs.text: The combustor case (210) holds the perforated liner (220), where fuel from the external lines (40) is burned in the compressed air.

paragraphs.heading: Turbine and exhaust
paragraphs.text: The turbine rotor (230) takes energy from the hot gas to drive the compressor and the fan. The exhaust cone (20) guides the gas into the nozzle.

paragraphs.heading: Case and mounts
paragraphs.text: The outer case (10) holds the sections in line and is joined at its flanges by the bolt set (50). The support ring (30) carries the engine and its thrust into the aircraft structure.

steps.title: Operation - overview
steps.text: Air enters at the front, is compressed, mixed with fuel and burned, and the hot gas drives the turbine before it leaves through the exhaust. The rotors turn on the shaft while this module is shown. Use Next to follow the air through the engine; the parts that do the work stay in colour.

steps.title: 1. Air enters the inlet
steps.text: The inlet guide vanes (120) turn the incoming air so that it meets the fan blades at the right angle.

steps.title: 2. The fan draws the air in
steps.text: The fan rotor (110) draws air into the engine. Part of it goes around the core as bypass air; the rest goes on to the compressor.

steps.title: 3. The compressor raises the pressure
steps.text: The compressor stages (130) squeeze the core air to many times the inlet pressure before it reaches the combustor.

steps.title: 4. Fuel is burned in the combustor
steps.text: The external lines (40) bring fuel to the nozzles in the combustor case (210). The fuel burns in the compressed air inside the perforated liner (220); cooling air flows in through its holes.

steps.title: 5. The hot gas drives the turbine
steps.text: The hot gas expands through the turbine rotor (230). The turbine turns the shaft that drives the compressor and the fan.

steps.title: 6. Exhaust and thrust
steps.text: The gas leaves past the exhaust cone (20) into the nozzle and produces thrust. The outer case (10) and the support ring (30) carry the thrust into the aircraft structure.

steps.title: Preliminary requirements
steps.text: Engine removed from the aircraft and installed on the engine maintenance stand. Fuel and oil drained. The removed parts are laid out in the order they come off.
steps.warning: WARNING: Let the engine cool down before you start. Hot section parts can cause burns.

steps.title: 1. Remove the exhaust cone
steps.text:
Remove the exhaust cone (tail cone) from the turbine exit.

Part details:
• Item 20 · Cone - Exhaust, Tail · P/N ENG-72-1020-02 - Exhaust (tail) cone at the turbine exit. Shapes the hot gas flow into the exhaust nozzle.

steps.title: 2. Remove the case flange bolts
steps.text:
Remove the nuts and bolts from the case flanges and the support ring. Keep the bolt sets together.

Part details:
• Item 50 · Bolt Set - Case Flange · P/N ENG-72-1050-01 - Bolts and nuts that join the case flanges and hold the support ring.

steps.title: 3. Remove the compressor disk assembly
steps.text:
Remove the compressor disk stack and put it on the rotor stand.

Part details:
• Item 130 · Disk Assy - Compressor Stages · P/N ENG-72-3130-01 - Compressor disk stack: the stages that compress the core air before it enters the combustor.

steps.title: 4. Disconnect and remove the external lines
steps.text:
Disconnect the fuel, oil and sense lines at their unions. Cap all openings, then take the tube assembly off.

Part details:
• Item 40 · Tube Assy - Fuel And Oil, External · P/N ENG-73-3040-01 - External fuel, oil and sense lines routed around the case to the fuel nozzles, bearings and sensors.

steps.title: 5. Remove the engine support ring
steps.text:
Support the engine on the stand, then remove the support ring.

Part details:
• Item 30 · Mount - Engine Support Ring · P/N ENG-71-2030-01 - Support ring and brackets that carry the engine on the aircraft mounts and take the thrust load.

steps.title: 6. Remove the combustor liner
steps.text:
Remove the perforated combustor liner.

Part details:
• Item 220 · Liner - Combustor, Perforated · P/N ENG-72-4220-01 - Perforated combustor liner: holds the flame and lets cooling air in through its holes.

steps.title: 7. Remove the combustor case
steps.text:
Remove the combustor case.

Part details:
• Item 210 · Case - Combustor · P/N ENG-72-4210-01 - Combustor case: pressure vessel around the combustion chamber that carries the fuel nozzles.

steps.title: 8. Remove the turbine rotor
steps.text:
Remove the turbine rotor stages from the shaft and put them on the rotor stand.

Part details:
• Item 230 · Rotor - Turbine, Bladed · P/N ENG-72-4230-01 - Turbine rotor stages: take energy from the hot gas to drive the compressor and the fan through the shaft.

steps.title: 9. Remove the fan rotor
steps.text:
Remove the fan rotor from the front of the shaft.

Part details:
• Item 110 · Rotor - Fan, Bladed · P/N ENG-72-3110-01 - Fan rotor: the first rotating blades at the engine inlet. Draws air in and sends part of it around the core as bypass air.

steps.title: 10. Remove the inlet guide vanes
steps.text:
Remove the inlet guide vane assembly.

Part details:
• Item 120 · Vane Assy - Inlet Guide · P/N ENG-72-3120-01 - Inlet guide vanes (stator): fixed vanes that turn the air onto the fan and compressor blades at the right angle.

steps.title: 11. Remove the outer case
steps.text:
The outer case is the last part left. Lift it off the stand. It stays in place in the layout: the other parts are laid out around it.

Part details:
• Item 10 · Case - Outer, Engine · P/N ENG-72-1010-01 - Outer engine case. Carries the bypass air and holds the compressor, combustor and turbine in line.

steps.title: Disassembly complete
steps.text: All parts are off the engine and laid out. Clean and examine each part before you assemble the engine again.

steps.title: Preliminary requirements
steps.text: All parts cleaned, examined and serviceable, laid out around the stand. Assembly is the disassembly in reverse order.
steps.caution: CAUTION: Use new self-locking nuts and seals. Torque all flange bolts to the values in the torque table.

steps.title: 1. Install the outer case
steps.text:
Put the outer case back in position and secure it.

Part details:
• Item 10 · Case - Outer, Engine · P/N ENG-72-1010-01 - Outer engine case. Carries the bypass air and holds the compressor, combustor and turbine in line.

steps.title: 2. Install the inlet guide vanes
steps.text:
Put the inlet guide vanes back in position and secure it.

Part details:
• Item 120 · Vane Assy - Inlet Guide · P/N ENG-72-3120-01 - Inlet guide vanes (stator): fixed vanes that turn the air onto the fan and compressor blades at the right angle.

steps.title: 3. Install the fan rotor
steps.text:
Put the fan rotor back in position and secure it.

Part details:
• Item 110 · Rotor - Fan, Bladed · P/N ENG-72-3110-01 - Fan rotor: the first rotating blades at the engine inlet. Draws air in and sends part of it around the core as bypass air.

steps.title: 4. Install the turbine rotor
steps.text:
Put the turbine rotor back in position and secure it.

Part details:
• Item 230 · Rotor - Turbine, Bladed · P/N ENG-72-4230-01 - Turbine rotor stages: take energy from the hot gas to drive the compressor and the fan through the shaft.

steps.title: 5. Install the combustor case
steps.text:
Put the combustor case back in position and secure it.

Part details:
• Item 210 · Case - Combustor · P/N ENG-72-4210-01 - Combustor case: pressure vessel around the combustion chamber that carries the fuel nozzles.

steps.title: 6. Install the combustor liner
steps.text:
Put the combustor liner back in position and secure it.

Part details:
• Item 220 · Liner - Combustor, Perforated · P/N ENG-72-4220-01 - Perforated combustor liner: holds the flame and lets cooling air in through its holes.

steps.title: 7. Install the engine support ring
steps.text:
Put the engine support ring back in position and secure it.

Part details:
• Item 30 · Mount - Engine Support Ring · P/N ENG-71-2030-01 - Support ring and brackets that carry the engine on the aircraft mounts and take the thrust load.

steps.title: 8. Install the external lines
steps.text:
Put the external lines back in position and secure it.

Part details:
• Item 40 · Tube Assy - Fuel And Oil, External · P/N ENG-73-3040-01 - External fuel, oil and sense lines routed around the case to the fuel nozzles, bearings and sensors.

steps.title: 9. Install the compressor disk assembly
steps.text:
Put the compressor disk assembly back in position and secure it.

Part details:
• Item 130 · Disk Assy - Compressor Stages · P/N ENG-72-3130-01 - Compressor disk stack: the stages that compress the core air before it enters the combustor.

steps.title: 10. Install the case flange bolts
steps.text:
Put the case flange bolts back in position and secure it.

Part details:
• Item 50 · Bolt Set - Case Flange · P/N ENG-72-1050-01 - Bolts and nuts that join the case flanges and hold the support ring.

steps.title: 11. Install the exhaust cone
steps.text:
Put the exhaust cone back in position and secure it.

Part details:
• Item 20 · Cone - Exhaust, Tail · P/N ENG-72-1020-02 - Exhaust (tail) cone at the turbine exit. Shapes the hot gas flow into the exhaust nozzle.

steps.title: Assembly complete
steps.text: The engine is assembled. Do the borescope inspection and an engine ground run before flight.

steps.title: Preparation
steps.text: Engine cold and on the stand. Open the borescope ports and connect the borescope.
steps.warning: WARNING: Make sure that the ignition is disarmed and the engine cannot be motored while the borescope is inserted.

steps.title: Fan and inlet guide vanes
steps.text: Examine the fan blades (110) and the inlet guide vanes (120) for nicks, dents and foreign object damage.

steps.title: Compressor stages
steps.text: Turn the rotor slowly by hand and examine each compressor stage (130) for blade damage and rubbing.

steps.title: Combustor liner
steps.text: Examine the perforated liner (220) for cracks between the cooling holes, burn-through and distortion.

steps.title: Turbine blades
steps.text: Examine the turbine blades (230) for tip erosion, coating loss and cracks. Record the findings with images.

steps.title: Close-up
steps.text: Remove the borescope, install the port plugs and record the inspection in the engine log.
